Michigan Secures Federal Grant for Broadband Expansion

Michigan-based fiber internet and voice provider 123NET has been awarded approximately $86 million in federal funding through the Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment (BEAD) program. According to the announcement, the funds are intended to accelerate high-speed fiber-optic installations across multiple underserved communities in the state.

The initiative is part of a broader effort involving the Michigan High-Speed Internet Office (MIHI) and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to bridge the digital divide. 123NET reported that it collaborated with local municipalities and community partners to secure the award, which targets thousands of locations as part of a larger network expansion.

Project Scope and Timeline

  • Funding Amount: Approximately $86 million allocated to 123NET.
  • Target Reach: 17,000 BEAD-funded addresses, contributing to a total planned network expansion reaching 49,300 addresses.
  • Infrastructure: Construction of 1,700 miles of new fiber network.
  • Impacted Counties: Allegan, Barry, Calhoun, Eaton, Jackson, Kent, Kalamazoo, Macomb, Monroe, Oakland, Ottawa, and Washtenaw.
  • Scheduled Start: Early 2027.

State officials noted that Michigan features the third-highest number of BEAD-eligible locations nationwide, supported by a combination of federal allocations and private-sector matching funds aimed at connecting nearly 200,000 homes, businesses, and institutions.

Practical Implications and Verification

Company executives stated that the infrastructure expansion aims to support economic development, remote education, and digital access for residents and small businesses currently lacking reliable connectivity. However, completing large-scale fiber deployments typically involves managing complex local permitting, deployment costs, and telecommunications workforce demands.

Residents living in the designated counties who want to check service availability or sign up for project notifications can visit the official 123NET Home Fiber Internet page. Program details and official state broadband maps can also be independently verified through the Michigan High-Speed Internet Office (MIHI).
